entry.title: Kotlin/Wasm: Accumulator Recursion Lowering
entry.summary: The pattern Some recursive functions wrap their self-call in an associative operator. fun countDown(n: Int): Int { if (n == 0) return 0 return 1 + countDown(n - 1) } countDown(n - 1) is not in tail position because 1 + wraps the result. -Xwasm-enable-tail-calls cannot help, and tailrec rejects this shape. entry.summary: Overview Tail Modulo Cons (Bour, Clément, Scherer) rewrites recursion whose result feeds a constructor into destination-passing style, turning the recursive call into a true tail call. OCaml 4.14 shipped this as [@tail_mod_cons]. PR 14 brings the same transformation to Kotlin/Wasm as @kotlin.wasm.TailModCons. entry.summary: Summary The Kotlin/Wasm tail call PR emits native Wasm return_call / return_call_ref at tail-position call sites. Microbenchmarks confirmed the expected speedup for deep recursion. However, applying the same compiler to four real Kotlin/Wasm workloads produced the opposite result on V8. Every workload either slowed down or stayed flat. The slowdown was a V8 bug.
